headline: All 115 interiors, both directions. A two-number definition of a good facing, the population baseline, a geometry-refined facing that takes exit failures 12 -> 2, and the camera arm counted and deliberately not claimed.
what_i_could_not_do: THE IN-BROWSER SWEEP OF ALL 115 DID NOT RUN. It is a stratified in-game sample of 16 interiors across 7 towns (the 12 the shipped data rule fails, plus barge-hold, blackrose-clerk, lilmoth-house-4 and helstrom-house-6 as controls), run in three arms. The POPULATION number comes from tools/world/door-yaw-offline.mjs, which runs the game's OWN modules (planSettlement/settlementSolids/interiorCollisionShapes/CollisionCell/exitFacing/entryFacing) in Node and is cross-validated against the running game row by row. Calling that a browser sweep would be false and it is not called one anywhere.

The contention gate read WAIT for essentially this whole pass (6-11 browser instances, load 26-45 over 4 cores). I proceeded past it with up to 3 browsers, which rule 21 permits provided it is said here: it is said here. A first attempt at the in-game sweep cost 610 s on a single row and was killed and restarted with the 36-bearing ceiling scan disabled (--no-best), which is the offline tool's job anyway.
No hardware (GPU) capture. Everything is SwiftShader on the local tree.
The deployed GitHub Pages site was NOT tested — Chromium in this container cannot reach any external host. Every number is the local tree.
The camera-arm collapse is measured and NOT fixed (see camera_arm_ruling below). It is the owner's original complaint surviving the facing fix, and it stays open.
The two wedged doorsteps (archon-vat-house, thorn-hall) are not fixed. They are defects in where the door was placed; thorn-hall's best possible clearance from its own doorstep is 2.5 m.
lilmoth-house-4's exterior spawn sees no geometry at all within 12 m on any of 36 bearings. Reported as an unknown, not a pass.
The Lilmoth camera-in-a-tree defect (D1) was not touched and is not merged with any of the above.

definition.clearance_m: distance to first solid at eye height (pos.y + 1.6), 0.25 m march, 12 m cap, via Engine.solidAt() = sim.cell.contains() — the collision set the body is depenetrated against and the camera arm casts into
definition.occluded_frac: share of 21 rays across the forward 60 deg (+/-30 deg, 3 deg apart) whose first solid is nearer than 3 m
definition.judged_on: sim.camera.yaw, with sim.player.yaw and combat.player.yaw recorded beside it
definition.frames: 1, 30 and 120 after the door verb, never one instant
definition.why_two_numbers: archon-vat-house has 12 m of clear sightline dead ahead and still fails, because 47.6% of the forward view is a wall at arm's length. Distance alone passes it.
definition.threshold_sensitivity: run over a 4x3 grid of thresholds; at every setting the data rule alone leaves 10-27 exits failing and the refinement takes it to 1-4. The result is not an artefact of the bar.

numbers.before_exit_any_prior: 1768 of 4140 (interior x prior-yaw) pairs fail = 42.7%; 114 of 115 interiors fail for at least one prior
numbers.after_geometry_refine_exit: 2 of 115 failing (predicted offline; confirmed in-game on archon-apothecary: 3.75 m / 0.286 PASS with the hook, 1.50 m / 1.00 FAIL without it)
numbers.facings_changed_by_the_refinement: 10 of 115; the other 105 are byte-identical in behaviour
numbers.camera_arm: 27 of 115 doorsteps leave the player below the fade threshold (out of frame); 33 shorten the arm; on 26 of the 27 some facing would clear it

the_fix.what: Engine._refineFacing() + Engine._facingCell(), reached through a new sim.faceRefine hook installed beside sim.placeBody / sim.applyCell / sim.doorVeto, consumed by sim/settlement.js#refineFacing() in useDoor() and leaveInterior().
the_fix.rule: the door record PROPOSES a facing; the collision set DISPOSES. Proposal passes -> returned unchanged, nothing scans. Proposal fails -> the nearest of 36 ten-degree bearings that passes wins. Nothing passes -> the proposal is kept, because a wedged doorstep is a placement defect and turning the player would hide it.
the_fix.why_not_data: authoring a continuity.exit_facing_deg for the twelve would be the third repeat of the frozen-derived-number shape that door_world_bearing_deg was already convicted of in reports/spawn-yaw/2026-08-14-door-exit-yaw.md.
the_fix.reversal: one line — remove the sim.faceRefine install in the Engine constructor. refineFacing() in settlement.js is fail-open by construction, so the tree falls back to the data rule. Executed on a clone as the `no-refine` teardown arm.
the_fix.cost: 103 of 115 doors cost one 21-ray fan; the 12 that fail cost up to 36 x 21 x 12 containment tests, once, at a door transition. Timed in the running game by tools/harness/door-yaw-consume.mjs.
the_fix.safe_under_the_determinism_guard: no wall clock, no load boundary; settlementSolidsNear() is the same pure call _settleSettlementSolids() already makes when the player moves 8 m.

camera_arm_ruling_reversible.ruling: the forward test is never traded away and the camera never overrides a facing that already clears. Rear clearance is used ONLY as a tie-break among bearings that already pass, on doors where the player is being turned anyway.
camera_arm_ruling_reversible.measured_both_ways: preferring a rear-clear facing whenever the proposal had none takes the fade count 27 -> 13, but turns the player at 26 exits instead of 10 and at 113 of 115 INTERIORS, because an interior spawn is against its own door wall by construction.
camera_arm_ruling_reversible.cost_of_the_ruling: two of the ten turned doors lose the camera to gain the facing — helstrom-house-11 and stormhold-customs go from 12 m rear to 0.5 m — so the fade count is 27 -> 29. Reported, not rounded off.
camera_arm_ruling_reversible.reversal: restore the `&& proposalRear >= FADE` clause in Engine._refineFacing() and the matching clause in predictRefine() in tools/world/door-yaw-offline.mjs. Both named in the source.
camera_arm_ruling_reversible.falsifier: somebody playing it and finding the invisible character worse than the unexpected turn, or the camera arm proving unfixable on its own terms.

instruments: tools/world/door-yaw-offline.mjs — the population: 115 x 2 in ~15 s, no browser, the game's own modules. Restates only Province._meshY(); validated against the running game with --validate.

tools/harness/door-yaw-sweep.mjs — the authority: the real useDoor()/leaveInterior() in the running engine, three yaw fields, frames 1/30/120, --entry to point an arm at a clone, --no-best to skip the ceiling scan.

tools/harness/door-yaw-teardown.mjs — five arms (before, no-refine, no-camera, mirror-only, no-combat). Every arm REFUSES to apply against a tree that does not contain the exact text, so an inert control is impossible; --self-test proves it and has already caught the tree moving under it once.
tools/harness/door-yaw-consume.mjs — RI-MTH07: four live arms (shipped / hook removed / hook perturbed +90 / restored) with a picture each and an 8-angle orbit.
next_step: collect the three in-game sweep arms; run door-yaw-consume for CONSUMPTION + screenshots; finish report section 7.
notes: game/src/engine.js edits are additive and narrow: a block of facing constants above the class, one hook-install line in the constructor, and two new methods immediately before _placeBody. Nothing pre-existing was rewritten.
The census hand-back framing in character/scene.js was NOT taken. Nobody should treat it as claimed by this piece.
